extraction.name: CIFAR-10
extraction.description: A labeled subset of tiny color images (32x32 pixels) containing 6000 examples of each of 10 classes, created from the larger 80 million tiny images dataset collected from the web. The dataset was designed for object recognition experiments with reliable class labels.
extraction.creator: Alex Krizhevsky
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected by groups at MIT and NYU over six months by searching the web for images of every non-abstract English noun in WordNet. Multiple search engines including Google, Flickr, and AltaVista were used, keeping roughly the first 3000 results for each search term. Perfect duplicates and images with excessively large portions of white pixels were removed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 80 million colour images downscaled to 32x32 pixels spread across 79000 search terms. The search term used to find an image provides it with a rough label, although it is extremely unreliable due to the nature of online image search technology.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Manual labeling to create reliable class labels for CIFAR-10 (6000 examples of each of 10 classes) and CIFAR-100 (600 examples of each of 100 non-overlapping classes). Labelers followed instruction sheet provided in Appendix C.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Search engines (Google, Flickr, Alta Vista) were used to collect images based on WordNet nouns, providing rough labels, though these are noted as extremely unreliable
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset exhibits strong correlations between nearby pixels and weak correlations between faraway pixels. Images tend to be symmetric about the vertical and horizontal axes, likely caused by the way people take photographs - making the ground plane horizontal and centering on the main object. The dataset contains biases from online image search technology, as search terms provide rough labels that are extremely unreliable due to the nature of online image search technology.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: A second problematic aspect of the tiny images dataset is that there are no reliable class labels which makes it hard to use for object recognition experiments. The search terms used to find images provide rough labels that are extremely unreliable. The dataset required creation of two sets of reliable labels (CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100) to enable object recognition experiments.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for unsupervised training of deep generative models to extract meaningful features. It is used for pre-training layers of features on unlabeled tiny images, which significantly improves object recognition. The labeled subsets (CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100) are used for object recognition experiments and classifier training.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were divided into 25 8x8 patches for training. A 26th patch was created as an 8x8 subsampled version of the entire 32x32 image. 26 independent RBMs were trained on each patch type and then merged into a single RBM.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were whitened using ZCA whitening transformation. The 1000 least significant principal components were deleted by setting corresponding entries in the diagonal matrix D to zero. For unwhitened experiments, data was preprocessed by deleting the 1000 least-significant directions of variance. Images were downscaled to 32x32 pixels. Perfect duplicates and images with excessively large portions of white pixels were removed.
